claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel Arthur H Onthank is Arthur Heath Onthank, the former War Department personnel director later documented as Lieutenant Colonel A. H. Onthank in OSS records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary appointment notice supplies the full name, while an NPS archival note links the initials, lieutenant-colonel grade, and OSS records.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an uncommon exact name, compatible rank progression, War Department chronology, and direct RG 226 context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place the civilian appointment in 1939-1941 and the lieutenant-colonel OSS-related role in July 1942.
claims.match_notes: Arthur Heath Onthank and A. Heath Onthank are retained as documented name variants.

claims.claim_text: Arthur Heath Onthank's last documented civilian government assignment before wartime military service was director of War Department personnel and chief of its Civilian Personnel Division.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The War Department announced his appointment in September 1939; an official Army history still identifies A. Heath Onthank as division chief in 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from uncommon name, compatible rank, and direct OSS-record context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded last civilian role before a July 1942 lieutenant-colonel assignment; no immediate OSS recruitment claim is made.
claims.match_notes: Government assignment is kept distinct from private employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Etienne Oostendorp is the Netherlands national whom an official 1945 State Department letter says OSS brought into the United States.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name appears in both the index and a direct official document describing OSS sponsorship.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, Netherlands-national context, and direct OSS linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1945 document establishes wartime identity but supplies no pre-OSS employer or sequence.
claims.match_notes: Conflicting birth years in unbridged local-history leads are not published or used for employment claims.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technical Sergeant Siegfried Oppenheim is the Master Sergeant later documented in OSS-related records and the Hoover Institution's Siegfried Oppenheim papers.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact protected-identifier match is independently corroborated by official and institutional records naming the same enlisted man in OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact protected identifier, exact name, compatible rank, and independent OSS documentation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The corroborating records concern OSS and postwar work; they do not establish pre-OSS employment.
claims.match_notes: An unbridged German-Jewish butcher with the same name is rejected as a namesake, not merged.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Arthur Oppenheimer is Arthur Oppenheimer Jr., documented as a 1942 Army enlistee and Captain serving as OSS Field Services Unit chief in November 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A federal digest supplies the full suffix and enlistment chronology; an OSS chart supplies the exact name, captain rank, and wartime role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from uncommon name, compatible rank progression, and direct official wartime documentation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources trace civilian service in April 1942, Army enlistment, and an OSS captain's role in November 1944.
claims.match_notes: Arthur Oppenheimer Jr. is retained as a documented name variant.

claims.claim_text: Arthur Oppenheimer Jr.'s last documented civilian government assignment before military service was chief of several Office of Price Administration household-goods units.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The federal Information Digest explicitly says he resigned the OPA role to enlist as a private in the Quartermaster Corps.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from official enlistment chronology and the later OSS chart.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate before military service; not asserted as the immediate pre-OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: OPA is a government assignment, not a private employer.

claims.claim_text: A June 1934 trade notice identifies Arthur Oppenheimer Jr. with Bloomingdale Brothers.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary periodical names him among drapery, upholstery, curtain, and allied-trades representatives and identifies his company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the distinctive full name and the separately documented wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment at one 1934 point; exact job title and duration are not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The profile does not inflate the trade notice into a buyer or executive title.

claims.claim_text: Arthur Oppenheimer Jr. enlisted as a private in the Army Quartermaster Corps in April 1942 before his documented OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The federal digest records the enlistment; the later OSS chart identifies him as Captain and Field Services Unit chief.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from official sources and compatible rank progression.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded pre-OSS military assignment, but not proved to be his final assignment immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment remains separate from civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Private Harry Oppenheimer is strongly consistent with the Harry Oppenheimer whom a family account in a reputable newspaper places with OSS in the Philippines in 1945.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence, while the undated family-business chronology remains insufficient for a pre-OSS employer claim.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source establishes wartime OSS context but does not reliably date the reported meat business before service.
